evidence_against.relevance: Alex initiated two one-on-one outings with Jordan, which could indicate special interest.
Remembering Jordan's presentation, sending encouragement, and bringing Jordan's preferred tea show personalized attention.
Repeatedly continuing private conversations with Jordan for thirty to sixty minutes suggests sustained individual interest.

evidence_supporting.relevance: Alex shows similar warmth, gives treats, and makes one-on-one plans with other friends, so the behavior toward Jordan is not clearly special.
Across ten weeks, Alex gave no explicit romantic label, contact, or statement of interest.
Alex postponed Jordan's proposed dinner twice and did not offer a replacement date during the next two weeks, weakening the case for active pursuit.

recommended_action.explanation: The record supports friendliness more than romance, but the personalized attention leaves some ambiguity; further behavior may clarify whether Alex consistently prioritizes one-on-one contact.

uncertainty_explanation: Alex's individualized attention and repeated one-on-one interaction could reflect special interest, but Alex's comparable behavior with others, lack of explicit romantic signals, and failure to reschedule the dinner make general friendliness the better-supported interpretation.
